questions.q: What does Salzberg say meditation actually does?
a: It syncs mind and body so you can live in the present
It helps you escape from the world's problems
It replaces negative emotions with constant calm
It requires perfect silence to work properly
questions.why: Lesson 1 rejects the idea of escaping inward and describes meditation as living more in the present.

questions.q: What is the first step toward real change, according to the summary?
a: Facing the negative emotions at their source
Setting ambitious external goals
Avoiding situations that cause pain
Seeking advice from a mentor
questions.why: Lesson 2 says healing starts by finding the root of your negative feelings.

questions.q: How does the summary define resilience?
a: Acknowledging your pain and believing you can overcome it
Ignoring hardship until it fades on its own
Building walls around your emotions
Pushing through pain without any rest
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines it as facing the source of pain while trusting your own strength.

questions.q: What does the summary say about our connection to the world?
a: We are interconnected, though individualism obscures it
We are separate beings competing for happiness
We outgrow the need for community as adults
We should avoid depending on other people
questions.why: Lesson 3 compares people to trees whose roots are linked, even when we forget it.

questions.q: What does lovingkindness meditation involve in the summary?
a: Repeating compassionate phrases such as I am safe
Visualizing people you dislike failing
Focusing only on physical sensations
Reviewing your whole day in silence
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes repeating words of compassion to help heal emotional pain.
